title: Effect of levothyroxine on left ventricular ejection fraction in patients with subclinical hypothyroidism and acute myocardial infarction: a randomized clinical trial
authors: Jabbar A, Ingoe L, Junejo S, Carey P, Addison C, Thomas H, et al.
population: Patients with acute myocardial infarction and persistent mild subclinical hypothyroidism in 6 UK hospitals; mean age 63.5 years, 76.6% men, median TSH 5.7 mU/l
funder: Dr Razvi was funded by an NIHR Career Development Fellowship (CDF-2012-05-231). The research was supported in part by the NIHR infrastructure at the University of Leeds. The funders had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
inKindSupport: Levothyroxine was provided free of cost by Amdipharm Pharmaceuticals UK Ltd.
authorConflicts: Dr Razvi reported nonfinancial support from Amdipharm during the study and personal fees from Merck and Abbott outside it; other authors reported fees from Abbott Vascular, AstraZeneca, Quidel, Sanofi and Berlin Chemie outside the submitted work.
result: Levothyroxine from 25 µg titrated to TSH 0.4 to 2.5 mU/l (n = 46) against placebo (n = 49). Left ventricular ejection fraction by MRI rose from 51.3% to 53.8% on levothyroxine and from 54.0% to 56.1% on placebo; adjusted difference 0.76% (95% CI -0.93% to 2.46%). None of 6 secondary outcomes differed. Cardiovascular adverse events: 15 (33.3%) on levothyroxine, 18 (36.7%) on placebo.
